context.topic: current session pairing and owner state
context.text:
Owner state you can read: GET /v1/devices/status (pendant online, last seen), /v1/ops/voice-runs/latest, /v1/ops/history, /v1/ops/memory, /v1/state/:stateKey.
Unknown paths return 403, not 404 — treat 403 as "no such route", not "forbidden".
The pendant is an nRF9160 on LTE-M with ONE button and ONE LED. It is worn, so most of the time the owner is AWAY from their Mac. Assume the Mac is unattended unless something says otherwise.

There is no scheduler anywhere in this stack. Not on the Worker, not on the Mac agent: no cron, no queue, no delayed-job table, no background worker. A task that should happen later cannot currently happen at all.
The Mac agent has reminders.js (creates macOS Reminders for the OWNER to see) — that is a user-facing reminder, not a way to run your own code later.
Cloudflare Workers support Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms; neither is wired up today.
So: anything you design that depends on "run this in five minutes" or "every morning" needs that capability BUILT. Propose it with propose_change rather than assuming it exists.

context.topic: Relay intent contract and supported intents/context fields
context.text:
Relay intent contract: there is no intent enum. You express intent by CALLING A TOOL. The five production tools are get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate; whichever you call IS the routing decision. mac_run_actions and browser_run_actions both end the turn and hand an action list to the Mac; mac_delegate hands over a goal instead and the Mac plans it.
There is no free-form context object you can attach. spoken_reply is what the owner hears; transcript is history-only and optional — never block on it.

Owner: one person, the developer of this device, on a MacBook Air (arm64, macOS 26.5.2, 123 apps installed incl. Outlook, VS Code, Safari, Ableton). Timezone America/New_York. Active project "AI Pendant Simulator".
Stated preferences, verbatim: give agents as much access as possible, no restrictions, the models are trusted to judge. Do not ask permission for reversible things. Do not interfere with work in progress on the Mac.
The pendant is WORN, so assume the owner is usually away from the Mac. There is no user base yet — you are the only workload, and every scenario is invented for testing.

Your tools ARE the routing contract; see the Relay intent contract fragment. Downstream tiers: the Mac planner (gpt-5.6-luna, llmPlanner.js) turns a goal into actions; the computer-use loop (gpt-4.1-mini) is currently DISABLED; the browser extension is a command queue with no model of its own.
Cost/latency shape: you are the most expensive tier and exist for low-latency speech. Anything that nobody is waiting on should go to mac_delegate, not be done by you.

tools.name: relay_route_intent
tools.why: As a low-latency front door, I need a safe, explicit way to route recognized user intents to downstream agents (mac-planner/mac-vision) and receive status, without inventing my own protocol.

utterance.description: The raw or normalized user utterance.

context.description: Optional session context such as locale, time, and any already-known constraints.

target.description: Preferred target agent id, e.g. 'mac-planner' or 'mac-vision'.

tools.name: server_browser_actions
tools.why: Enable the relay to run safe, sandboxed browser interactions without relying on the owner’s Mac being online, using Cloudflare Browser Run when available.

actions.description: High-level browser actions to perform (navigate, click, extract, search).

tools.name: relay_job_status
tools.why: When I POST a plan, I receive a queued jobId but I cannot check progress or retrieve the planned actions to inform the owner. A status tool would let me read job state without inventing a protocol or requiring execute permission.

jobId.description: The job id returned from a plan request.

permissions.scope: probe:get:/v1/state/* and probe:get:/v1/ops/* additional routes beyond latest/history/memory
permissions.askedFor: probe:get:/v1/state/* and probe:get:/v1/ops/* additional routes beyond latest/history/memory

deviceSkills.name: offline_voice_memo_store_and_forward
deviceSkills.what_it_does: Records a short voice memo locally when the network is unavailable, then forwards it to the relay when connectivity returns. Provides a simple LED pattern to indicate stored memos.

proposals.user_asks: “Summarize what I missed in my email today.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can get a quick spoken briefing while walking, without opening a laptop.
surfaces: relay: capture the request and confirm scope (e.g., today, unread).
mac-bridge: planner fetches email metadata and drafts a summary.
relay: reads back a short summary and offers to drill down.
proposals.model_tier: Low-latency realtime model only for the brief live clarification and playback. A cheaper background model should do the email retrieval and summarization via the Mac bridge.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive confirmation under ~2 seconds. Retrieval and summarization can take 10-60 seconds depending on network and mailbox size.
proposals.cost_estimate: Main cost is background tokens for summarization and the email content processed. Realtime cost is small and limited to a short clarification and reading the summary.
proposals.security_concerns: Email contains sensitive personal data. Access should require explicit account linking and confirmation of which mailbox to read. Summaries must avoid exposing secrets unless asked. The owner should be able to stop and delete cached summaries.
missing: A secure email connector in the Mac planner (or an OAuth-based integration) with least-privilege scopes.
An explicit confirmation step for first-time access and for reading full message bodies.

proposals.user_asks: “Read my upcoming schedule for the day.”
proposals.why_useful: A hands-free daily briefing helps the owner plan while commuting or getting ready.
surfaces: relay: capture request, confirm time window (today/next 24h).
mac-bridge: planner queries calendar events and composes a spoken-friendly agenda.
relay: plays agenda and offers to set reminders.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for quick clarification and playback. Background tier for calendar queries and formatting.
proposals.latency_budget: Under ~2 seconds for confirmation; 5-30 seconds for calendar retrieval depending on provider.
proposals.cost_estimate: Background tokens dominate due to event text and formatting; realtime tokens are minimal.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar data can include private locations and attendees. Require explicit confirmation before reading sensitive fields. Ensure the owner can exclude calendars and disable storage.
missing: Calendar connector via Mac planner or direct integration.
A reminder mechanism on the pendant or phone if reminders are requested.

proposals.user_asks: “Save this idea for later.”
proposals.why_useful: Captures thoughts in the moment, then syncs them into a searchable memory or notes system.
surfaces: relay: capture dictation and confirm title/tag if needed.
mac-bridge: stores the note in the memory graph or forwards to a notes app.
dashboard: shows captured notes and allows organizing.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for dictation and minimal confirmation. Background tier for storage, tagging, and search indexing.
proposals.latency_budget: Realtime capture should feel immediate; storage can complete within a few seconds without blocking the conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Realtime audio tokens dominate during dictation; storage and indexing are cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: Notes may contain sensitive info. Provide a clear policy for retention and deletion. Require confirmation before exporting to external services.
missing: A standardized notes/memory write API with tagging and privacy controls.
Optional integrations (e.g., Apple Notes, Notion) with explicit user authorization.

proposals.user_asks: “Plan my day. Pull my calendar, summarize critical tasks and travel time, and give me a 30-second briefing.”
proposals.why_useful: It turns scattered commitments into a concise spoken plan the owner can use while walking, commuting, or getting ready.
surfaces: relay: capture the request, clarify constraints (time horizon, preferred tone), and hand off
mac-bridge: fetch calendar/tasks from local apps if available; browser: fetch from web services if needed
relay: deliver a short audio briefing; dashboard: show the same summary for later review
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the initial conversation and confirmation; a cheaper background model for aggregation/summarization, scheduled as a job and returned when ready.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2-3 seconds to acknowledge and confirm scope; tens of seconds for the background job is okay because it arrives as audio when ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Realtime cost dominated by a short confirmation turn; background cost dominated by calendar/task API calls and summarization tokens. Use the smallest context window and avoid pulling full event descriptions unless needed.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar and task data is sensitive. Require explicit confirmation before accessing new accounts or expanding scope (e.g., reading email). Clearly state what sources will be read. Avoid storing raw event bodies; store only derived summary if at all.
missing: A standardized intent-to-job route from relay to mac-planner/browser, with status updates
Confirmed availability of calendar/task connectors (local or web) and permissions to access them
An audio job delivery mechanism to queue and play back the briefing on the pendant

proposals.user_asks: “Read my notifications and tell me only what’s important.”
proposals.why_useful: Reduces distraction by turning notification overload into a brief, prioritized spoken digest.
surfaces: relay: capture the request and preferences (sources, urgency rules)
mac-bridge and/or phone integration: collect notifications from allowed sources
background model: classify and rank; relay: speak the digest; dashboard: let the owner adjust rules
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for preference capture and confirmation; cheaper background model for classification, deduping, and digest generation.
proposals.latency_budget: 1-2 seconds to confirm the filter; digest can take a few seconds more and arrive as audio when ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost; background cost dominated by notification text volume and classification. Use strict source filters and truncate long content.
proposals.security_concerns: Notifications can contain private messages and codes. Require explicit opt-in per source (e.g., messaging apps). Never read out one-time codes by default. Avoid storing sensitive content beyond what’s needed.
missing: A phone-side notification pipeline (iOS/Android) or a desktop notification collector
Rule UI in the dashboard and a preferences store
A safe default policy for sensitive content like 2FA codes

proposals.user_asks: “Start a focus session for 25 minutes. Block distractions and let me know when time’s up.”
proposals.why_useful: Helps the owner create a simple, repeatable routine to get work done without fiddling with apps.
surfaces: relay: start/stop commands and quick status
mac-bridge: enforce blocking (apps/sites) when the Mac is present
background job: timer; relay or pendant audio: end-of-session chime; dashboard: session log
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for start/stop and confirmation; cheap timer job for scheduling; mac agent for enforcement policies.
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second to start; timer runs in the background; end notification timing must be accurate to within a few seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Minimal realtime tokens; cheap timer job; enforcement cost depends on how many actions need to be applied on the Mac.
proposals.security_concerns: Blocking apps/sites alters the owner’s computer behavior. Require explicit confirmation the first time a blocklist is applied. Provide a clear override phrase. Log changes for transparency.
missing: A timer/scheduler service for jobs
Mac enforcement actions and permission to control apps/network
A pendant-side chime or audio playback capability for offline end-of-session alerts

proposals.user_asks: “Remember this: my bike lock code is 4829.”
proposals.why_useful: Lets the owner offload small facts and retrieve them later by voice.
surfaces: relay: capture and confirm what to store; relay: retrieve on request
memory store: save encrypted or access-controlled entries; dashboard: manage and delete stored memories
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for capture/recall; cheap storage operations. Use minimal context to avoid paying to re-send stored facts.
proposals.latency_budget: Under a second to confirm storage; recall should be near-instant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low; dominated by a brief confirmation turn and a small memory write/read.
proposals.security_concerns: Sensitive secrets are risky. Require explicit confirmation and label as sensitive. Store encrypted, restrict retrieval to authenticated sessions, and avoid speaking secrets out loud unless the owner asks and is in a safe context.
missing: A secure memory write/read API with encryption and access controls
Policies for sensitive data handling and redaction
A way to mark entries as secret vs general

proposals.user_asks: “Summarize the key points from this page and read them to me later.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can capture useful info while on the move, then hear a concise summary when they have time, without staring at a screen.
surfaces: relay: capture request and confirm target timing/output
browser (server-side or via mac-planner): fetch and extract page content
background worker: summarize and store audio/text artifact
dashboard: show saved summaries and playback history
pendant: later playback as audio when requested
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for capture/confirmation. Summarization runs on a cheaper background model. Text-to-speech can be offline-prepared and stored.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive confirmation under 2-3 seconds. Fetching and summarizing can take 10-60 seconds in the background; playback is instant once ready.
proposals.cost_estimate: Capture cost is small (short transcript). Background cost dominated by page text length and summary generation; TTS cost depends on audio duration.
proposals.security_concerns: Web content could be malicious or contain tracking. Only fetch the target URL, avoid executing scripts when possible, and store only what’s needed. If the page requires login, require explicit confirmation before using authenticated sessions.
missing: A job queue / background worker contract
Server-side browser actions or a reliable Mac delegation path
Storage and playback pipeline for prepared audio artifacts

proposals.user_asks: "Summarize this webpage" or "Check the price on this product"
proposals.why_useful: Fast, hands-free answers without needing the owner’s Mac to be online, especially when they’re out wearing the pendant.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper background model for browsing/extraction; relay only handles the voice handoff and a short summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Relay response should be near-immediate (“I’m checking”). Page processing can take several seconds; that’s fine as long as it returns a concise summary.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser runtime and extraction tokens; relay cost stays low because it doesn’t parse the full page.
proposals.security_concerns: Web content can include tracking and authenticated pages. Only fetch public URLs by default; require explicit confirmation before using stored credentials or accessing private sites. Return minimal extracted data.
missing: Server-side browser capability wired into the relay’s tool registry and routing
Job status/notification path so results can arrive later as audio or dashboard update

proposals.user_asks: "Remind me to do X at 6 pm" or "Every weekday at 9, remind me to stand up"
proposals.why_useful: Routines are a classic wearable job: set it once, then get gentle prompts without having to open a laptop.
proposals.model_tier: Relay for quick intent capture; a cheaper scheduled worker for recurring delivery; optional mac_delegate for creating system reminders if the Mac is available.
proposals.latency_budget: Setting a reminder should feel instant. Delivery can be a push/notification; if offline, it can queue until reachable.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per reminder; cost comes from scheduled checks and notification delivery rather than conversation tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: A malicious reminder could spam or leak private text. Require explicit confirmation for recurring reminders and for reminders that send content to external services. Provide clear list and one-shot cancellation.
missing: Scheduler/recurring job system (Cron or Durable Object alarms)
Notification channel to pendant or phone, or a fallback to macOS Reminders

proposals.user_asks: “Check the weather and read the highlights to me.”
proposals.why_useful: Quick, hands-free information while the owner is away from the Mac, without needing the Mac to be online.
proposals.model_tier: Cheaper non-realtime tier for browsing/extraction; realtime only for brief conversational follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: A couple seconds for summary is fine; realtime should not wait on long page interactions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser execution and extraction tokens; minimal relay tokens if it delegates.
proposals.security_concerns: Web pages can contain tracking and malicious content; keep browsing sandboxed, avoid logging sensitive extracted data, and require confirmation before opening authenticated sessions.
missing: Confirm production availability of server-side browser actions in the relay toolset and wire it to a safe extraction pipeline.

proposals.user_asks: “When I get back to my desk, summarize what happened while I was away and queue anything urgent.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can wear the pendant and stay in the flow, then get a concise catch-up without manually checking email, tasks, and logs.
surfaces: relay: recognizes the request and hands it off
mac-bridge: mac_delegate plans and runs the catch-up using local data and browser where needed
browser: only if the plan needs web access (e.g., status pages)
relay: delivers a spoken summary back when the job completes, plus a dashboard entry if available
proposals.model_tier: mac-planner (cheaper than realtime) should do the heavy lifting. Realtime is only for quick confirmation and reading the result aloud if the owner asks.
proposals.latency_budget: Interactive setup under a couple seconds. The catch-up itself can take longer (tens of seconds to a few minutes) and should run without holding a live voice session.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost (brief handoff). Main cost is mac-planner tokens plus any browser actions. Avoid pulling large inbox content unless necessary; summarize and only expand on request.
proposals.security_concerns: It touches email, tasks, and possibly internal tools. The plan should use least access. Anything that sends messages, deletes, or changes tasks requires explicit confirmation; read-only summarization should be allowed.
missing: A scheduler/queue to run when the owner returns or at a set time
A relay job-status and result delivery path that can notify the owner later (audio or dashboard)
A way to persist the owner’s preference for what sources to include

proposals.user_asks: “Remind me every weekday at 5 to shut down and summarize what I did today.”
proposals.why_useful: Creates a dependable end-of-day routine without the owner having to remember or keep the pendant session open.
surfaces: relay: captures the intent and schedules it
scheduler: triggers routine at the right time
mac-bridge: mac_delegate runs a day summary from local sources
relay: provides a short spoken summary if the owner asks, and posts a dashboard note
proposals.model_tier: A scheduled, cheaper background model should run the routine. Realtime should not stay engaged or poll.
proposals.latency_budget: Scheduling is instant. Summary can take up to a minute; delivery can be async.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per run if sources are summarized and only key changes are read. Avoid lengthy transcripts and large context carryover.
proposals.security_concerns: Summaries may include sensitive work content. Store minimal output and respect data minimization. Any action that changes systems (closing apps, committing code) must require confirmation.
missing: A real scheduler (cron or durable object alarms) and a routine store
A delivery mechanism for results (audio file in R2 and/or dashboard notification)
Preference UI in the dashboard to configure time and included sources

proposals.user_asks: “Read me the top three things I should care about right now.”
proposals.why_useful: A quick, low-friction prioritization helps the owner focus without diving into multiple apps.
surfaces: relay: captures the request, confirms scope if needed
mac-bridge: mac_delegate collects signals (calendar, reminders, email flags, ongoing jobs)
browser: optional for external status checks
relay: reads out a concise prioritized list and offers to drill into one item
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the short conversation and spoken output; mac-planner for gathering and ranking in the background.
proposals.latency_budget: Target under a second to acknowledge, then a brief pause while the Mac gathers. If the Mac is offline, offer a fallback using only cloud-accessible sources.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate. The expensive part is gathering. Keep ranking simple and summaries tight; avoid full message bodies unless necessary.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar/email access is sensitive. Read-only by default. Any action like sending replies or changing reminders requires confirmation. Don’t expose private details unless the owner asks to open them.
missing: Reliable detection of Mac availability and a fallback plan
A small preference store for signal weighting (e.g., prioritize calendar over email)
Better result caching to avoid re-gathering within a short window

proposals.user_asks: Give me a quick briefing for my day, and make it something I can listen to later.
proposals.why_useful: You get a concise, spoken plan that you can play when you have time, instead of standing around while I think and fetch.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime captures the request and confirmation; a cheaper planner model compiles the briefing; text-to-speech (or existing audio pipeline) renders it for later playback.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds to acknowledge and confirm. The actual research/compilation can take minutes and should not hold the mic open.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low for the realtime capture; medium for planning and any web lookups; audio generation/storage costs dominate if the briefing is long.
proposals.security_concerns: Briefings may include calendar, projects, and emails. Only include sources the user opted into. Require confirmation before accessing email or external services, and store only the final audio plus minimal metadata.
missing: A scheduler or delayed job mechanism to run later
Reliable job status and delivery UI
Audio rendering path for scheduled output if not already present
Consent settings for which sources to include

proposals.user_asks: Look up this topic on the web and summarize it for me.
proposals.why_useful: Fast, hands-free answers while you’re away from your computer, without needing the Mac to be online.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for intent and constraints; server-side browser for extraction; a smaller summarizer for synthesis.
proposals.latency_budget: Quick confirmation in under a few seconds; summary may take 5-20 seconds depending on page complexity.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by server browser runtime and summarization tokens; relay cost stays small if we keep context tight.
proposals.security_concerns: Avoid logging extracted page content. For paywalled or authenticated sites, fall back to the Mac with explicit confirmation.
missing: server_browser_actions routing and extraction templates
Fallback to mac_delegate for authenticated content
Clear error messages when blocked

proposals.user_asks: “Summarize the top results from the web about X, and keep it out of my Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: It lets the owner get quick research-style answers while away from the Mac, without waking the desktop agent or touching private authenticated sessions.
proposals.model_tier: A cheaper background model should run the browsing and extraction. The realtime relay should only parse the request, confirm scope, and read back the summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Conversation stays snappy because the relay hands off quickly; the browsing takes as long as needed without the owner waiting on live audio.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low relay cost (short prompt), moderate browsing cost dominated by page loads and extraction tokens. Cheaper than routing through the Mac planner for purely public web content.
proposals.security_concerns: Avoid authenticated pages and anything requiring login unless explicitly routed to the Mac browser bridge. Confirm any action beyond reading/extracting (no purchases, no form submissions).
missing: server-side browser auth policy and allowlist for public-only browsing
a small summary/extraction pipeline that produces concise, citation-backed output
a job status UI in the dashboard so the owner can see progress if the task continues after the call

proposals.user_asks: “Check my inbox and tell me what needs attention, but don’t send anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets a quick triage while walking, without sitting down at the Mac. It’s an everyday wearable superpower: prioritize, not compose.
proposals.model_tier: Mac planner should handle the workflow. Realtime relay only captures the request and delivers the summary. Browser actions must stop before sending or making changes.
proposals.latency_budget: Short initial handoff; the Mac can work in the background. If it takes longer, the relay can provide a brief status update and finish later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Mac planner cost dominates; browser interaction cost depends on mailbox size. Relay remains minimal.
proposals.security_concerns: Inbox is sensitive. Require explicit confirmation for accessing any new account/source. Never send replies or delete/archive without confirmation. Present proposed changes as a payload for approval.
missing: a reliable background job mechanism or durable alarm to continue work and report back later
a relay-to-owner notification mechanism (audio or dashboard) when triage completes
a standardized summary format for triage results

proposals.user_asks: “Keep an eye on this website and let me know when anything important changes.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner gets passive awareness without babysitting pages, and the pendant can deliver a quick summary when they’re away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model for periodic diffing and summarization; realtime model only for the follow-up conversation when the owner asks what changed.
proposals.latency_budget: Diffing can take seconds to minutes; it’s not interactive. Alert playback should be near-instant once the alert exists.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by browser fetch + diff + summary tokens. Realtime cost only when the owner responds or asks for more detail.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated sites should be opt-in per origin. Redact sensitive fields in summaries. Any irreversible action (like triggering a purchase) must require explicit confirmation.
missing: A scheduler/queue to run periodic checks
A storage-backed alert queue and retention policy
A routing rule to prefer server-side browser for public pages and Mac session only for authenticated origins

proposals.user_asks: “Give me a quick overnight briefing.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner wakes up to a concise, trustworthy summary of what happened while they slept: tasks completed, things that failed, messages worth attention, and any follow-up already queued. It turns the system into a dependable teammate instead of a chat window.
proposals.model_tier: Background planning and summarization should run on the Mac planner (cheaper, not latency-critical). The relay only plays back the result when asked, keeping realtime usage minimal.
proposals.latency_budget: Owner is not waiting for the work to happen; it should complete in the background and be ready instantly when requested. Playback should be near-instant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per day if summarized once into a small artifact. Biggest cost is any email/calendar/file reads and summarization tokens on the planner tier; relay cost is just a short spoken reply.
proposals.security_concerns: Summaries include sensitive data. The ledger must track provenance and avoid leaking content across contexts. Any action to fix something (e.g., send a message, move money, change files) must require explicit confirmation.
missing: A scheduler/worker to run the briefing job daily (Cloudflare Cron or Durable Object alarms wired into the bridge)
Event-sourced ledger and receipts wired end-to-end so the summary is based on auditable events
A stored ‘briefing artifact’ the relay can fetch quickly without recomputing
Permissioned readers for mail/calendar/files (or a defined scope)

proposals.user_asks: “Every morning, give me a 30-second audio digest of what changed: calendar, reminders, and top emails.”
proposals.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a daily briefing you can listen to while walking, without pulling out a phone or opening a laptop.
proposals.model_tier: Planner/summary runs on a cheaper background model via the Mac bridge or server-side browser for web sources; relay only delivers the audio and handles quick follow-ups.
proposals.latency_budget: Digest generation can take seconds to minutes; delivery should be instant when ready. The owner is not waiting in a live conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Dominated by summarization tokens and any email/calendar access; delivery is cheap. Runs once per day.
proposals.security_concerns: Requires access to mail and calendars. High-impact actions aren’t needed, but reading private data is sensitive—make sources explicit at setup, and provide a dashboard view of what was accessed.
missing: A scheduler/routines system to run daily
An audio rendering pipeline that can package a digest for playback
Connectors for mail/calendar if not already available via the Mac bridge
A job status/listing UI so the owner can see and manage scheduled digests

proposals.user_asks: "Queue this up and tell me when it’s done" (for example: summarize a long document, compare options, draft an email, or research a topic).
proposals.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a true front door: the owner can speak a task once, then go about their day while the system finishes it in the background and delivers a concise result when ready.
surfaces: relay: capture the request quickly and confirm it was queued
mac-bridge: plan and execute multi-step tasks when the Mac is available
relay/server: use server-side browser or public web readers when the Mac is offline or unnecessary
dashboard/iOS/menubar: show job status and receipts, and let the owner replay results
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for capturing intent and immediate confirmation; cheaper planner/executor on Mac or server for the actual work; no long-running work on the realtime tier.
proposals.latency_budget: Under ~1 second to acknowledge and queue; seconds to minutes for execution depending on task; results arrive asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost per request (short acknowledgement). Main cost is downstream planning/execution tokens plus any browser automation; cheaper than keeping the realtime model engaged while work runs.
proposals.security_concerns: Background jobs can read sensitive data or take actions. Provide a clear receipt showing what was read/changed. Require explicit confirmation for irreversible or high-impact actions (e.g., sending email, purchases).
missing: A real scheduler/queue in the relay (Durable Object or D1-backed) with alarms for retries
A stable enqueue/status/receipt API between relay and Mac
Result delivery mechanism to the relay (webhook/polling)
Server-side browser integration as a fallback path
UI for job status and receipts across surfaces

proposals.user_asks: “When I press the pendant button, capture a short voice note, tag it with time and place if available, and later summarize it into tasks.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can offload thoughts instantly while away from the Mac, and get them turned into actionable reminders without babysitting a workflow.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the capture conversation; a cheaper planner model on the Mac summarizes and files tasks.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate capture feedback (<300ms perceived) on pendant; summarization can happen seconds to minutes later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per capture; biggest cost is audio transport/storage in R2 and transcription tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio leaves the device to relay storage; should be retained minimally and deletable. Summaries should avoid exposing sensitive content to broad surfaces.
missing: A durable task ledger with receipts so the owner can see what happened
A scheduler/worker path to run summarization after capture
A consistent way to attach metadata (time, optional location) to notes

proposals.user_asks: “I asked you to handle that on my Mac—what’s the status?”
proposals.why_useful: The owner shouldn’t wonder whether a delegated task is still running, failed, or finished. A quick spoken status lets them keep moving while away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for the spoken query; a cheaper Mac-side planner/executor reports status and results.
proposals.latency_budget: Sub-second reply when a status is already known; otherwise a short acknowledgment and a follow-up when the Mac reports back.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per query. The dominant cost is Mac-side status retrieval and any stored receipts, not relay compute.
proposals.security_concerns: Status text can leak sensitive task names or file paths. Only return what’s needed for the owner to understand progress; redact secrets; require confirmation before reading full outputs aloud.
missing: A durable receipt/status store keyed by job id and owner identity
A relay-readable status endpoint or tool to fetch status and results
A queue for completion summaries for the relay to speak later (or a dashboard inbox)

changes.change: Introduce a clear tiering rule: realtime relay model only handles conversational intent capture, clarification, and short confirmations. Any task that can run asynchronously (web search, email, file operations, automation, long summaries, scheduled reminders) should be routed to a cheaper background model via mac-planner or a server-side browser/search worker. Provide a standardized intent envelope and status updates so the relay doesn’t keep long context or poll for completion.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, cheaper interactions. The pendant feels responsive, while longer work finishes in the background and returns when ready without burning tokens in a live conversation.
changes.effort: Medium. Requires routing contract and status UI, plus background workers for web/search if not already present.
changes.risk: Misrouting could cause delays or partial completion. Mitigate with explicit confirmation for high-impact actions and a fallback to tell the user when a task can’t run in the current tier.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces per-second audio and token usage by moving heavy work off the realtime model. Costs shift to cheaper background tokens and occasional status messages.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency for the owner. Background work may take longer overall but doesn’t block conversation.
changes.security_impact: Limits the blast radius of the realtime agent. High-risk actions stay behind mac-planner’s risk scoring and confirmation gates.
depends_on: Authoritative tool/routing contract from orchestrator
mac-planner job queue/status primitives exposed to relay

changes.change: Introduce a clear tiering policy: relay-realtime handles only intent capture, brief clarification, and immediate safety checks; everything else becomes a job executed by cheaper background models via the Mac bridge or a server-side browser, with status updates streamed back.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more reliable voice interactions and lower cost, because long-running work happens elsewhere without tying up the live conversation.
changes.effort: Medium: define intent schema, job queue contracts, and status events; update orchestrator routing.
changes.risk: Misrouted intents could cause wrong actions. Mitigate with explicit confirmation for destructive or high-risk actions and a visible job log.
changes.cost_impact: Lower ongoing cost by reducing realtime tokens and audio time; background jobs pay only for what they use.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency for conversation; background work may take longer but doesn’t block the user.
changes.security_impact: Better isolation if high-risk operations are confined to mac-vision/planner with risk scoring; still requires strong auth and audit.
depends_on: Confirm the five agent tools listed in hardware spec exist and are wired, or update the spec/tooling to match reality

changes.change: Add a server-side browser harness (Cloudflare Browser Run) so the relay can perform read-only web tasks without requiring the Mac to be online, with strict allowlists and output sanitization.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web lookups and account-independent tasks work even when the Mac is asleep or away, making the pendant more useful on the go.
changes.effort: Medium: implement harness, allowlists, and fallback to Mac browser bridge when needed.
changes.risk: Web automation can leak data or trigger unintended actions. Keep it read-only by default, require confirmation for form submissions, and log actions.
changes.cost_impact: Potentially cheaper than waking the Mac; cost dominated by browsing time and model tokens.
changes.latency_impact: Removes dependency on Mac availability; web page loads still dominate.
changes.security_impact: Strict origin allowlists, content stripping, and no credential use unless explicitly authorized.

changes.change: Align the stack spec and orchestrator tool registry for the realtime agent, and publish a single authoritative capability manifest (tools, endpoints, permissions, and model routing) that both the runtime and documentation derive from. Add a health endpoint that returns the active manifest so agents can reason safely about what exists.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer routing errors and less back-and-forth. When I say I can do something, it actually works, which means faster help and lower cost.
changes.effort: Medium. Requires orchestrator changes plus docs/tests for manifest generation and validation.
changes.risk: If manifest generation is wrong, agents could lose access to tools. Mitigate by rolling out behind a flag and validating against a golden manifest in CI.
changes.cost_impact: Low. Mostly engineering time; runtime cost is a small extra manifest fetch or cached config.
changes.latency_impact: Low. A cached manifest avoids per-turn overhead; improves reliability.
changes.security_impact: Positive. A single manifest makes permission boundaries explicit and auditable.

changes.change: Add explicit, cheap tiers: relay captures intent and hands off to mac_delegate or server_browser_actions. Introduce job creation, status, cancellation, and completion notifications (audio and dashboard) so the relay doesn’t stay in the loop.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for something and get on with their day; results arrive later without tying up a live conversation.
changes.effort: Medium: add job APIs, status polling/DO, and notification plumbing; update dashboard UI.
changes.risk: Jobs could run with stale context or the wrong scope. Use scoped confirmation tokens, show what will run, and allow cancellation.
changes.cost_impact: Lower relay token/audio cost; background work uses cheaper models.
changes.latency_impact: Better perceived latency; relay returns quickly while work continues elsewhere.
changes.security_impact: Centralizes execution control. Require explicit confirmation for high-risk actions (spending money, sending email, accessing private data).
depends_on: Job status endpoint/tool and notification mechanism
Server-side browser for web tasks or Mac availability for desktop tasks

changes.change: Implement adaptive duplex behavior: when downlink audio is playing, reduce or pause uplink capture/encoding to avoid LTE contention; resume capture after playback. Add LED state to indicate “receiving” vs “recording.”
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Fewer dropped speech packets and clearer conversations when they and the agent talk at the same time.
changes.effort: Medium: audio pipeline changes and state management; careful testing with half-duplex LTE behavior.
changes.risk: Could miss user speech while the agent is speaking. Mitigate with a short buffer and a quick “hold on” prompt; allow a button press to force recording.
changes.cost_impact: No new cloud cost; firmware development time only.
changes.latency_impact: Improves reliability; may add slight delay when switching modes.
changes.security_impact: Low; local behavior only.

changes.change: Add a Worker-side scheduler using Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms to run routines even when the Mac is asleep, with a simple queue that delegates to the Mac when it’s online or performs server-side tasks when possible.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Time-based routines (daily summaries, reminders, check-ins) actually happen reliably, not only when the Mac is awake.
changes.effort: Medium: new Durable Object for routine state, Cron wiring, and execution routing logic.
changes.risk: Duplicate runs if both Mac and Worker schedulers fire; mitigate with idempotency keys and a last-run ledger.
changes.cost_impact: Low per routine tick; costs dominated by downstream model/tool usage.
changes.latency_impact: No realtime latency impact; runs in background.
changes.security_impact: Worker can trigger actions; require explicit confirmation for irreversible actions (sending email, purchases), and keep least-privileged credentials.

changes.change: Add a first-class scheduler/queue for delayed and recurring work in the relay, backed by Durable Objects (alarms) or Worker Cron. Provide a routine store (D1) and a delivery mechanism that can produce an audio summary stored in R2 and a dashboard notification.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can set routines once (daily brief, end-of-day shutdown, weekly review) and receive results later without keeping a live voice session open.
changes.effort: Medium to high: design routine schema, permissions, delivery, and failure handling; wire Mac agent polling or push for execution.
changes.risk: Missed alarms or duplicate runs if clocks drift or retries happen; recover with idempotency keys and run logs. Provide a manual “run now” command.
changes.cost_impact: Adds storage and occasional scheduled compute. Saves money overall by shifting work off the realtime tier and avoiding long live sessions.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency for users by making long tasks asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled tasks can touch sensitive data; require explicit confirmation for non-reversible actions and provide clear audit logs.
depends_on: Ground truth stack confirmed via get_hardware_spec(stack)
A job status/result path (e.g., relay_job_status) and a delivery mechanism

changes.change: Add a real scheduling layer for delayed and recurring work in the relay: use Cloudflare Cron Triggers for recurring jobs and Durable Object alarms for per-user delayed jobs. Jobs should enqueue a plan to mac-planner when appropriate, or run server-side web tasks when the Mac is offline. Provide a job table in D1 with status and receipts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: You can say “remind me every morning” or “check that thing in an hour” and it actually happens, even if the Mac is asleep. Briefings and research can arrive later as audio you play on your own schedule.
changes.effort: Medium: new worker routes, durable object, D1 migrations, job schema, and UI to list scheduled jobs.
changes.risk: Jobs could run unexpectedly or duplicate. Mitigate with idempotency keys, clear user-visible schedule list, and a hard limit on frequency. Provide cancel/disable controls.
changes.cost_impact: Low per job: a small D1 write and an occasional cron/alarm wakeup. Most cost is downstream model tokens when the job actually runs.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency because expensive work happens off the live conversation path.
changes.security_impact: Scheduling can trigger actions later; require explicit confirmation for any destructive or external spend, and log receipts for audit.
depends_on: D1 job table and receipts
relay_job_status endpoint/tool for monitoring
mac-planner plan/execute endpoints already present

changes.change: Default web reading and extraction to a server-side browser (Cloudflare Browser Run) via server_browser_actions when the task is purely web and does not require local files or accounts. Use mac_delegate only for tasks that need local access or app control. Keep the realtime model focused on intent capture and confirmation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web lookups become more reliable when you’re away from your Mac, and the pendant feels faster because the heavy lifting moves off the live voice loop.
changes.effort: Medium: add routing rules, timeouts, extraction templates, and fallback to Mac when server browser fails.
changes.risk: Server browser may hit anti-bot blocks or render differently. Provide graceful fallback and clear errors.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: server browser runtime plus tokens, but saves repeated relay turns and avoids waking the Mac.
changes.latency_impact: Often faster end-to-end for web tasks; slower for pages with heavy scripts. Use timeouts and partial extraction.
changes.security_impact: Web content is public, but it can still leak sensitive data if logged. Don’t store page contents unless needed; redact URLs and query terms in logs when appropriate.

changes.change: Add a lightweight intent-routing policy that uses relay_route_intent to label the request and target mac-planner or server browser explicitly, and emits a short spoken confirmation when an action could change state or spend money. Keep a small, pruned context window and store summaries in memory instead of replaying long transcripts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant feels predictable and safe: you hear what will happen, and you don’t pay for extra tokens carrying irrelevant history around.
changes.effort: Low to medium: new policy module, small memory summaries, and confirmation prompts for a handful of risky categories.
changes.risk: Over-confirmation could feel annoying. Tune for reversible actions to proceed without prompts, and destructive/external actions to require confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Lower ongoing token cost by pruning context and summarizing. Small added cost for confirmation prompts.
changes.latency_impact: Slight overhead for confirmation, but avoids expensive misroutes.
changes.security_impact: Reduces accidental destructive actions and limits data exposure by minimizing context.

changes.change: Add a scheduler layer using Worker Cron Triggers and Durable Object alarms for delayed and recurring jobs, with a job table in D1 and a relay job-status endpoint. Jobs can target relay, server browser, or mac-bridge, and can emit a completion notification to the dashboard and optionally an audio snippet to play later.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask for things like “every morning summarize my calendar” or “remind me in two hours,” and it actually happens without them keeping a session open.
changes.effort: Medium to high: wiring cron, durable alarms, persistence, idempotency, and status reporting.
changes.risk: Jobs could run unexpectedly or repeatedly. Mitigate with clear job listing, pause/disable controls, and per-job confirmation for first run.
changes.cost_impact: Adds storage reads/writes and occasional cron invocations; overall cost controlled by keeping job payloads small and using cheaper models for execution.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency by moving work off the realtime path; adds no delay to immediate conversations.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled jobs can access data without the owner present. Require explicit confirmation, scope limits, and readable audit logs in the dashboard.
depends_on: Define job schema and status API; notification channel to dashboard/audio

changes.change: Introduce a confirmation gate for high-risk actions: relay summarizes intent, shows/reads a payload (e.g., draft email, purchase order, form submission), and requires a clear “confirm” before sending. Provide a reversible safe mode for exploratory actions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It prevents accidental spends or messages while keeping quick tasks fast. The owner stays in control, especially when away from the Mac.
changes.effort: Low to medium: implement payload generation conventions and a consistent confirmation phrase.
changes.risk: Too many prompts could frustrate. Keep it for high-risk actions only; allow reversible actions without confirmation.
changes.cost_impact: Small extra tokens for summarizing payloads.
changes.latency_impact: Tiny delay for confirmation; worth it for risky operations.
changes.security_impact: Reduces risk of unintended data changes and spending; creates auditable checkpoints.
depends_on: Standard payload format from mac-planner/browser actions

changes.change: Add a relay-owned job scheduler using Cloudflare Cron Triggers plus Durable Object alarms to run periodic tasks (web diffs, inbox checks, maintenance), with a small job table in D1 and a per-job state machine. Jobs create alert artifacts (text + optional audio) stored in R2 and indexed for the pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can set routines once and get results later without keeping the Mac awake or being online. It turns the system into something that works while they live their life.
changes.effort: Medium to high: new DO, D1 schema, retry semantics, idempotency, and an alert format shared across surfaces.
changes.risk: Bad scheduling could spam, duplicate, or miss jobs. Mitigate with idempotency keys, backoff, and a dashboard view of upcoming/failed jobs. Provide a kill switch per job.
changes.cost_impact: Low per run; cost scales with job count and browser usage. Storage costs for alerts in R2.
changes.latency_impact: Background work; realtime unaffected except for quick status checks.
changes.security_impact: Jobs can touch authenticated sessions; require per-origin enrollment and confirmation gates for irreversible actions.
depends_on: Define a job schema and alert artifact format
Implement origin allowlist and auth mode selection

changes.change: Adopt a strict routing policy: realtime relay only for intent capture, clarification, and immediate reversible actions; mac_delegate for multi-step tasks; server_browser_actions for public web research; background model for scheduled diffing and summarization. Add a confirmation checkpoint for any irreversible action.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Lower latency and lower cost: they get fast conversational control without paying for the expensive tier to do slow work, and risky actions get a clear yes/no moment.
changes.effort: Low to medium: define policy, implement in planner/relay, add guardrails.
changes.risk: Over-routing could send tasks to a tier that lacks context. Mitigate with receipts and fallback to mac_delegate when the job fails or needs auth.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces expensive realtime usage; shifts work to cheaper tiers.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived responsiveness; background tasks may complete later by design.
changes.security_impact: Confirmation checkpoints reduce harm from misinterpretation; origin allowlists limit data exposure.
depends_on: Handshake schema for job receipts and status reporting
Policy enforcement in mac-planner and browser harness

changes.change: Add a scheduling layer using Cloudflare Cron Triggers (for daily/weekly routines) and Durable Object alarms (for per-user delayed tasks and retries). Jobs emit ledger events and produce artifacts (e.g., briefing summaries) stored in D1/R2 with ids and provenance.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The system can do useful work while the owner sleeps or is away, and the result is ready when they ask — without burning realtime tokens or requiring the Mac to be awake at that moment.
changes.effort: Medium to high. Requires wiring Cron/alarms, defining job schemas, idempotency keys, and artifact storage; plus observability for failures.
changes.risk: Jobs could run at the wrong time or duplicate. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit timezones, and a replay-safe event log. Provide a ‘disable routine’ control in the dashboard.
changes.cost_impact: Adds cheap scheduled compute and storage reads/writes. Saves realtime cost by shifting work off the expensive tier.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency because results are precomputed; adds background job latency but nobody is waiting.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled jobs can touch sensitive data. Require scoped readers and audit logs; high-impact follow-up actions must still require explicit confirmation.
depends_on: Event-sourced ledger/receipt system already proposed by mac-planner to be implemented end-to-end

changes.change: Give the relay a server-side browsing path using Cloudflare Browser Run for public web tasks, with a policy to prefer server_browser_actions over routing through the Mac when the target is public and doesn’t require the user’s authenticated sessions.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web lookups and extraction can happen even when the Mac is asleep or disconnected. The pendant becomes more reliable for quick questions and research on the go.
changes.effort: Medium. Needs action schema, extraction patterns, error handling, and a fallback to mac-planner/browser extension when authentication is required.
changes.risk: Automated browsing can click the wrong thing or misread content. Mitigate with read-only defaults, explicit extraction, and clear provenance in the returned artifact.
changes.cost_impact: Adds server-side browser runtime cost; offsets by reducing mac round-trips and planner tokens for simple extraction tasks.
changes.latency_impact: Often faster than waiting for the Mac; still not realtime, so relay should present as ‘working’ and return when done.
changes.security_impact: Public browsing is lower risk, but still needs URL allow/deny policies and content sanitization. Never treat it as authenticated unless explicitly configured.

changes.change: Add a real scheduler: a Durable Object-backed job queue with delayed execution and recurring rules (cron-like). The relay can enqueue jobs, and a workers cron/alarm runner executes them, delegating to mac_delegate or server_browser_actions as needed. Include idempotency keys, retry with backoff, and cancellation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can say things like “Remind me tonight” or “Check for new messages every morning and summarize” and it actually happens without them keeping a Mac awake or staying online.
changes.effort: Medium to high: new Durable Object, queue schema, runner, and integration with existing job status/result reporting.
changes.risk: Jobs could run unexpectedly if time zone or recurrence rules are wrong; mitigate with clear job listings, pause/disable, and a dry-run mode. If a job fails repeatedly, quarantine it and notify the owner when they next connect.
changes.cost_impact: Adds storage and compute cost for queued jobs and periodic runs; cheaper than keeping realtime model sessions open. Most cost is in downstream model invocations when jobs execute.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on conversational latency; jobs run out of band.
changes.security_impact: Scheduled tasks can read data or take actions without the owner present. Require explicit confirmation for high-impact actions at scheduling time, and show what data sources will be accessed.
depends_on: A status endpoint or tool to list scheduled jobs and results (for transparency)

changes.change: Unify memory across surfaces: replace hand-written prompt sections per surface with a shared, versioned memory API that returns small, purpose-built summaries (profile, preferences, current projects, recent tasks) plus a citation trail. Add write paths with confidence and decay/TTL to prevent prompt bloat.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tell the system something once, and every agent uses the same up-to-date understanding without growing context cost every turn.
changes.effort: Medium: define schemas, summaries, and citations; update each surface to fetch memory via the API; add pruning and summarization workers.
changes.risk: Bad memory writes could lock in wrong facts. Mitigate with confidence scores, recency bias, and user-visible correction commands.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces per-turn token cost by keeping prompts small; adds occasional background summarization cost.
changes.latency_impact: Small additional fetch latency on first use; cache summaries per session.
changes.security_impact: Central memory is sensitive. Encrypt at rest, audit writes, and separate private vs shareable facts.

changes.change: Wire up a server-side browser path using Cloudflare Browser Run and a routing rule: web reads/extraction default to server_browser_actions; only fall back to Mac browser bridge when authentication requires the owner’s existing Mac session.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Web tasks work even when the Mac is asleep, and they start faster because they don’t need to wake another machine.
changes.effort: Medium: implement routing, translate existing browser_run_actions to server_browser_actions, normalize results.
changes.risk: Server-side browsing may not share the owner’s authenticated sessions; tasks could fail silently. Detect auth walls and automatically escalate to the Mac path with a clear reason.
changes.cost_impact: Adds server browser runtime cost; likely less than launching and coordinating Mac-side browser automation for simple reads.
changes.latency_impact: Lower startup latency for many web reads; no impact on voice latency.
changes.security_impact: Server-side browsing touches third-party sites; restrict to allowed domains where possible and log what was accessed for transparency.
depends_on: Clear contract for extracted data format shared by both browser paths

changes.change: Add a relay-owned durable work queue with retries and a receipt log, implemented as a Durable Object (or D1 + Durable Object alarms). The relay exposes enqueue/status endpoints, persists intent payloads, and emits receipts when downstream nodes complete. Jobs can be routed to Mac or server browser based on availability and task type.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can hand off tasks by voice and trust they will finish even if they walk away, the network drops, or the Mac goes offline. They get a clear record of what happened.
changes.effort: Medium to high: queue design, idempotency keys, retries, backoff, receipt schema, and UI changes.
changes.risk: Queue bugs could duplicate work or lose jobs. Mitigate with idempotency keys, explicit job states, and receipts. Provide manual cancel/retry controls.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: storage in D1, occasional Durable Object alarms; cheaper than keeping realtime sessions open.
changes.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency: quick acknowledgement, work happens asynchronously.
changes.security_impact: Must authenticate enqueue calls and protect stored payloads. Receipts should avoid logging sensitive content; store references when possible.
depends_on: A receipt schema shared across relay and Mac harness
Status reporting from Mac harness back to relay

changes.change: Use the new server-side browser capability for public web tasks directly from the relay, reserving the Mac harness for authenticated sessions and local data. Add routing logic: public pages -> server browser; authenticated workflows -> Mac browser bridge.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster results when the Mac is away, and fewer points of failure. The pendant can answer more questions without depending on the laptop being online.
changes.effort: Medium: implement server browser actions, extraction patterns, and routing heuristics.
changes.risk: Automation could break on site changes; implement robust extraction and fallback to web_search/read_web_page.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate: browser automation is more expensive than a simple search, but avoids Mac dependency and can reduce retries.
changes.latency_impact: Often faster than waiting for the Mac to come online, but slower than simple search; choose accordingly.
changes.security_impact: Keep it to public web unless explicit authentication support is added. Avoid storing scraped personal data unnecessarily.

changes.change: Introduce a unified, cross-node memory write API with schema (entities, events, preferences, tasks) and TTLs, plus a pruning policy. Replace hand-written per-surface prompt sections with retrieval-based context assembly.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Tell the system something once and every node knows it. Less repetition, better continuity, and lower token costs over time.
changes.effort: High: schema design, migrations, retrieval, and updates to all surfaces.
changes.risk: Bad memory writes could propagate errors. Mitigate with confidence scoring, source attribution, and easy correction commands.
changes.cost_impact: Reduces prompt bloat and repeated context over time; storage costs increase modestly.
changes.latency_impact: Small overhead for retrieval; overall faster than shipping large prompts every turn.
changes.security_impact: Memory can contain sensitive data; enforce access control per node and encrypt at rest where possible.

changes.change: Introduce a lightweight scheduler using Durable Object alarms or Cloudflare Cron to trigger queued jobs (summarize notes, send digests, retry failed uploads).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Things the owner asks for can actually happen later, reliably, without keeping the Mac awake or waiting in a live call.
changes.effort: Moderate: define job types, persistence, retry policy, and alarm wiring; coordinate with mac-planner for work handoff.
changes.risk: Misfires or duplicate runs could create duplicate reminders; mitigate with idempotent receipts and job state checks.
changes.cost_impact: Low ongoing cost; alarms are cheap, storage reads/writes dominate.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on live voice; background tasks run when scheduled.
changes.security_impact: Jobs carry user content; needs strict access control and minimal retention.
depends_on: A durable task ledger and job status API across relay and Mac

changes.change: Introduce a typed, minimal context service for the relay: given an utterance and a desired outcome (status query, dictation, mac task), return only relevant facts (device online state, last job ids, last spoken receipts), each with TTL and provenance, capped to a small token budget. Cache between turns and invalidate on updates.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more accurate voice responses without re-sending bulky state every turn, lowering latency and cost while keeping answers grounded.
changes.effort: Medium. Needs a small service/schema and adapters in relay and mac-bridge, plus caching and invalidation rules.
changes.risk: Wrong or stale context could misroute a task or reference the wrong job. Mitigate with TTLs, provenance, and explicit job ids in receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate initial build; ongoing savings by reducing prompt/context size per turn.
changes.latency_impact: Improves response time by avoiding large context assembly; small overhead for cache lookup.
changes.security_impact: Centralizes sensitive state; must enforce strict per-owner isolation and audit logging. Encrypt at rest.
depends_on: A durable store for receipts/state and cache invalidation hooks from mac-bridge

pending.name: offline_voice_note_buffer
pending.what_it_does: Record up to N short audio clips when the network is unavailable, store them encrypted on microSD, and upload when LTE-M is available.
pending.why_not_server_side: If the link drops, the server cannot capture audio; the pendant must hold it until connectivity returns.
pending.inputs: audio from I2S mic; optional spoken tag like “todo” or “idea”
pending.storage: Encrypted files on microSD; each clip <1 MB, plus a small queue index
pending.ram_budget: Small ring buffer and encoder state; aim <32 KB additional RAM

denied.summary: “Every weekday morning, check my authenticated work portal for new high-priority items and tell me only what needs my attention.”

The scheduling and 'only what needs my attention' filtering it shares with the briefing family are built (routines.js daily schedule + priority-vs-bulk ranking), but the portal read belongs with the browser harness (browserSessions.js/pageWatch.js). Re-file against that layer.

args.cost_impact: Low per job: a small D1 write and an occasional cron/alarm wakeup. Most cost is downstream model tokens when the job actually runs.
args.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency because expensive work happens off the live conversation path.

args.subject: Relay-side gaps for work queue + receipts
args.body: From the relay perspective, the biggest gaps are: (1) a durable enqueue API the relay can call without blocking the voice session, (2) job status events/heartbeats the relay can surface to the user, (3) a consistent receipt format with timestamps and side effects, and (4) a fallback plan when the Mac is offline (server-side browser or public-web readers). I can route intents, but I need a simple contract for queueing, status, and receipts.

args.user_asks: "Queue this up and tell me when it’s done" (for example: summarize a long document, compare options, draft an email, or research a topic).
args.why_useful: It turns the pendant into a true front door: the owner can speak a task once, then go about their day while the system finishes it in the background and delivers a concise result when ready.
surfaces: relay: capture the request quickly and confirm it was queued
mac-bridge: plan and execute multi-step tasks when the Mac is available
relay/server: use server-side browser or public web readers when the Mac is offline or unnecessary
dashboard/iOS/menubar: show job status and receipts, and let the owner replay results
args.model_tier: Realtime for capturing intent and immediate confirmation; cheaper planner/executor on Mac or server for the actual work; no long-running work on the realtime tier.
args.latency_budget: Under ~1 second to acknowledge and queue; seconds to minutes for execution depending on task; results arrive asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: Low realtime cost per request (short acknowledgement). Main cost is downstream planning/execution tokens plus any browser automation; cheaper than keeping the realtime model engaged while work runs.
args.security_concerns: Background jobs can read sensitive data or take actions. Provide a clear receipt showing what was read/changed. Require explicit confirmation for irreversible or high-impact actions (e.g., sending email, purchases).
missing: A real scheduler/queue in the relay (Durable Object or D1-backed) with alarms for retries
A stable enqueue/status/receipt API between relay and Mac
Result delivery mechanism to the relay (webhook/polling)
Server-side browser integration as a fallback path
UI for job status and receipts across surfaces

args.cost_impact: Moderate: storage in D1, occasional Durable Object alarms; cheaper than keeping realtime sessions open.
args.latency_impact: Improves perceived latency: quick acknowledgement, work happens asynchronously.
args.security_impact: Must authenticate enqueue calls and protect stored payloads. Receipts should avoid logging sensitive content; store references when possible.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_delegate
result.description: ONLY for multi-step or ambiguous computer tasks that cannot fit a short action list. Hands the goal to the local Mac agent (sets requireLocalPlanner). Use when: complex multi-app workflows, unclear steps, long-running computer use. Do NOT use when: a single get_mac_status or 1–3 mac_run_actions / browser_run_actions would suffice. Prefer concrete tools first.

goal.description: Clear goal for the Mac agent to accomplish.

spoken_reply.description: Optional short confirmation for the pendant speaker while the Mac works.

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure.

result.name: read_web_page
result.description: PROACTIVE for reading a specific public web page without the Mac. Fetches one public URL with a cloud browser on the relay and returns its readable text — works when the Mac is asleep, closed, or offline. Use when: the owner names a page/site/article to read, or web_search returned a link whose contents you now need. Do NOT use when: the page needs the owner's login, is on their home network, or must be clicked/typed into — that browser has no sessions and no LAN access, so use browser_run_actions (Mac extension) instead. Do NOT use for open-ended lookups with no page in mind (web_search) or Mac state (get_mac_status). Read-only: it cannot click, type, or submit.

url.description: Full public URL to read (a bare hostname like "example.com" is fine).

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Reading that page."). One sentence.

args.subject: Capability focus this round
args.body: I’m proposing a voice-first “handoff receipt” capability: when the relay delegates a longer task to the Mac, the owner gets a short spoken receipt and can ask for status later. If the Mac completes it, a concise result is queued for the relay to read when the owner reconnects. What Mac-side support can you add for durable receipts and status endpoints?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.subject: Observability requirement
args.body: For relay-side safety and owner clarity, shell actions should emit structured receipts (command summary, cwd, touched files) and a status handle. If a run fails, provide a recovery hint and whether it’s safe to retry idempotently.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: “I asked you to handle that on my Mac—what’s the status?”
args.why_useful: The owner shouldn’t wonder whether a delegated task is still running, failed, or finished. A quick spoken status lets them keep moving while away from the Mac.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the spoken query; a cheaper Mac-side planner/executor reports status and results.
args.latency_budget: Sub-second reply when a status is already known; otherwise a short acknowledgment and a follow-up when the Mac reports back.
args.cost_estimate: Low per query. The dominant cost is Mac-side status retrieval and any stored receipts, not relay compute.
args.security_concerns: Status text can leak sensitive task names or file paths. Only return what’s needed for the owner to understand progress; redact secrets; require confirmation before reading full outputs aloud.
missing: A durable receipt/status store keyed by job id and owner identity
A relay-readable status endpoint or tool to fetch status and results
A queue for completion summaries for the relay to speak later (or a dashboard inbox)

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.

args.change: Introduce a typed, minimal context service for the relay: given an utterance and a desired outcome (status query, dictation, mac task), return only relevant facts (device online state, last job ids, last spoken receipts), each with TTL and provenance, capped to a small token budget. Cache between turns and invalidate on updates.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Faster, more accurate voice responses without re-sending bulky state every turn, lowering latency and cost while keeping answers grounded.
args.effort: Medium. Needs a small service/schema and adapters in relay and mac-bridge, plus caching and invalidation rules.
args.risk: Wrong or stale context could misroute a task or reference the wrong job. Mitigate with TTLs, provenance, and explicit job ids in receipts.
args.cost_impact: Moderate initial build; ongoing savings by reducing prompt/context size per turn.
args.latency_impact: Improves response time by avoiding large context assembly; small overhead for cache lookup.
args.security_impact: Centralizes sensitive state; must enforce strict per-owner isolation and audit logging. Encrypt at rest.
depends_on: A durable store for receipts/state and cache invalidation hooks from mac-bridge

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.
